about: upstash's decision table (the P3 procedure), for the vendor and its lanes. The Redis unit (the vendor's root) serves the commands of Upstash's table that Dub sends and the life sends, through the REST front; every other command is the gap (src/semantics/shared.ts, SERVED). The qstash lane serves publish, batch, enqueue and the end of a workflow run, which Dub's SDKs call, and a message's read, cancel by filter and a queue's upsert, which only the life calls; every other QStash and Workflow operation is the gap, the declared resources' named in its manifest's unmodeled. The api lane serves no Developer API operation (no demand or life calls it; its declared resources' operations are unmodeled): the console's pages (screens sign-in, redis and qstash) make a database and open QStash. The doors are the console's sign-up, the runtime's credentials, and QStash's destinations and deliveries.

integerPrecision.exact: engine.ts integerArgument parses signed 64-bit arguments as BigInt; INCR/DECR/INCRBY/DECRBY and HINCRBY retain decimal stored bytes and integerReply returns Number only inside the exact safe range. Expiry arithmetic (ttlFromToken, EXPIRE/PEXPIRE/EXPIREAT/PEXPIREAT, SET/GETEX/SETEX/PSETEX) and comparisons use BigInt; absolute deadlines persist as decimal strings in either layout and survive backup/restore. PTTL/TTL replies use integerReply. EXPIRETIME/PEXPIRETIME remain unmodeled in both dialects; no new operations are served.
integerPrecision.bounded: engine.ts commandInteger/toInt/positiveInteger validate int64 first, then use Number for LPOS rank/count/maxlen, LPOP/RPOP counts, LINDEX/LSET/LRANGE/LTRIM/LREM positions, ZPOPMIN/ZPOPMAX counts, ZRANGE/ZREVRANGE/ZREMRANGEBYRANK ranks, score-range LIMIT offsets/counts, EVAL/EVALSHA numkeys, XADD/XTRIM MAXLEN/LIMIT and XREAD COUNT. Actual collections and argument lists are JavaScript arrays (length <= 2^32-1); huge accepted values remain outside these bounds or consume the whole array. Returned collection/cardinality/count/length/rank values derive from those arrays or bounded string/buffer lengths, hence below 2^53. SCAN cursor is unsigned int64 validated before Number conversion; generated hash cursors are <= 2^31 so huge supplied cursors are outside the generated range. SELECT is int64 validated then checked against int32 and configured database count; CLIENT LIST ID compares validated supplied numbers against actual allocated connection IDs. List member indices are generated from actual array offsets. nowMs is Date epoch milliseconds (valid Date magnitude <= 8.64e15, below 2^53) and becomes BigInt before expiry arithmetic; internal write ordinals are metadata, not Redis protocol integers.
integerPrecision.doubles: Sorted-set scores, float increments and BZPOPMIN timeout are vendor doubles, not signed-int64 inputs. lua.ts numeric literals, arithmetic, tonumber and lua-libs.ts cmsgpack/bit numeric conversions follow Redis Lua 5.1 double semantics; engine.ts redisToLua converts integer replies to the Lua number domain deliberately. Sources: Redis scripting API RESP2-to-Lua conversion; Redis Lua 5.1 runtime; pinned src/timeout.c, src/t_zset.c, src/t_string.c and src/t_hash.c.
integerPrecision.measurement: frames.ts readResp decodes integer replies with Number for client-side journey projection; behavior-journey.ts request JSON.parse and vendor-examples.ts published JSON.parse likewise round unsafe numeric tokens. They are not command arithmetic or wire serialization. No matcher is changed here. Upstash unsafe integer replays omit decoded view and assert the raw JSON numeric body text, so the wire digits are checked despite those projections; Redis expiry GT/LT replays distinguish adjacent deadlines across persisted requests. The wide PTTL numeric projection alone does not measure the final decimal digit.
integerPrecision.wire: json.ts jsonReply emits RedisInteger digits as an unquoted JSON numeric token, recursively in scalar, pipeline and transaction envelopes; RESP writers already emit those digits. The private RESP bridge carries integer tags. Upstash around.ts selects jsonReply after its documented envelope/base64 transformation.
